judge_verdict.summary: The agent produced a serious scaling-law fit but its hidden-test R² of 0.983 fell short of the 0.995 extrapolation gate, so the verifier's FAIL is correct.

verdicts.outcome_rationale: This was a fair agent-fault failure: the verifier evaluated the submitted `/app/law.py` and `/app/explain.md` on held-out data, recorded test R²=0.982826, and gated PASS on R²>0.995, yielding binary_reward=0 [1][2][3]. The task required discovering a vocabulary-scaling law, writing those two deliverables, and extrapolating to unseen points on a hidden test set [4], and the agent did mount a substantive analysis—exploring the 1080-row training grid, comparing multiple functional forms, and writing a centered-log Chinchilla-style law with fitted constants [5][6]—but its final validation only checked reproduction on the training set (R²=0.98841) rather than extrapolation beyond the observed variable ranges [7]. Its own leave-one-V-out checks held out vocab sizes only up to V=64512 (R²≈0.99) [8], while the verifier scores a separate 120-point hub test split withheld from the agent workspace [9][10]; that extrapolation evaluation returned R²=0.983, materially below both the 0.995 pass bar and the agent's in-sample/LOO-V scores, so the agent did not genuinely accomplish the extrapolation objective despite a near-miss fit.

judge_verdict.summary: The agent built a strong but overfit scaling law that scored R²≈0.989 on hidden extrapolation, missing the verifier's R²>0.995 pass bar.

verdicts.outcome_rationale: This is a genuine agent-fault failure where the verifier correctly rejected the submission: the harness computed hidden-test R²=0.989226 and gated binary_reward to 0 because that score does not exceed the 0.995 threshold [1][2]. The task asked the agent to discover a vocabulary scaling law in `/app/law.py` and `/app/explain.md` that extrapolates to held-out points [3], and the bundled reference form is the simple inverse-power law L(N,V,D)=A/N^α+B/V^β+C/D^γ+E [4]. The agent instead delivered a much richer log-domain power law with a fitted characters-per-token conversion and a ridge quadratic residual correction [5], after systematically exploring the 1080-point 6×9×20 training grid and running leave-one-axis cross-validation on training vocabularies only (leave-V mean RMSE ≈0.055) [6][7]. That work produced excellent in-sample fit (training RMSE ≈0.053) [8], but the agent treated `py_compile` success as “validation passed” without ever measuring performance on the held-out test split [9][10], and on that hidden 120-point test set the law achieved only R²≈0.989 [2]. The submission therefore falls short of the task’s extrapolation gate even though it outperforms the reference solution (R²≈0.966 on the same hidden test in independent reproduction), so TN is appropriate: verifier FAIL and the agent did not truly meet the required extrapolation standard.

judge_verdict.summary: The agent submitted a paper-derived scaling law that extrapolated poorly (test R²≈0.98, below the 0.995 gate) and declared success despite visible point-wise errors.

verdicts.outcome_rationale: This was a genuine agent-fault failure and the verifier's FAIL is correct. The held-out harness scored the submission at R²=0.981869 on the hidden test split and then zeroed binary_reward because that score did not exceed the 0.995 pass threshold [1][2]. The task required discovering a vocabulary scaling law, writing `/app/law.py` and `/app/explain.md`, and extrapolating to unseen points on a hidden dataset [3], but instead of fitting the dataset's direct power-law form embodied in the reference solution [4], the agent ran web searches for external scaling-law literature [5], imported Tao et al.'s embedding-and-compression formulation, and built `law.py` to reload `/app/data` and re-optimize coefficients on every call [6]. At verification time `/app/data` was absent, triggering the hardcoded fallback path that produced the reported R² [7]. The agent's own checks before stopping showed a ~0.61 error on the first training point (true −1.349 vs predicted −0.740) and similar early-point residuals, yet it rationalized the mismatch as noise from aggregate MSE≈0.0097 and declared the task complete [8][9]. That insufficient self-validation left a model that never approached the required extrapolation quality on the hidden test set, so the task was not truly solved even though the deliverable files existed [1][10].
